questions.question: Emergency equipment, such as fire extinguishers, is required:

options.text: Only in vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, turn the steering wheel:

options.text: In the direction you want the trailer to go.
In the opposite direction from where you want the trailer to go.
To the left until you finish backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the opposite direction from where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system:

options.text: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can let poisonous fumes into the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab. Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: An improperly placarded vehicle:

options.text: Can only be moved in an emergency.
Can be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper hazmat placards cannot be driven, except in an emergency to protect life and property.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, the ____ trailer should be right behind the cab.
questions.explanation: The heaviest loaded trailer should be closest to the tractor. The lightest trailer should be at the rear.

questions.question: During an engine compartment check, you should not:
questions.explanation: During an engine inspection, check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level, but do not drain brake fluid.

questions.question: More than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents are caused by:
questions.explanation: Rollovers cause more than half of truck driver deaths. To prevent rollovers, keep cargo low and centered. Take corners slowly.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:
questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage to your vehicle.

questions.question: In cool weather, as ice begins to melt:

options.text: It is usually safe to drive.

questions.explanation: As ice melts, water sits on top of the ice and makes the road more slippery. Slow down and be careful on slippery roads.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes.
A valve that shows the fuel level.
A valve that limits cargo weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar is a hand valve used to test the trailer brakes. Use it only for testing. Using it while driving can cause a skid.

questions.question: During a CDL vehicle inspection test, you may be asked to:
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you need to check the engine oil level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: Shaded areas of a road:

options.text: Are blocked from moisture and cannot freeze.
Stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and warm up slowly. They stay icy and slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.question: On any uphill grade, gravity will:
questions.explanation: Gravity slows your vehicle down on uphill grades. You may need to shift to a lower gear to climb a steep hill.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each night to stay alert?
questions.explanation: To drive safely, you need proper rest. Most adults need eight to nine hours of sleep each night to stay alert.

questions.question: Lower the risk of jackknifing by:
questions.explanation: Avoid skidding by steering, speeding up, and braking smoothly. If the drive wheels or trailer wheels start to skid, the vehicle could jackknife.

questions.question: You should not use your mirrors to:

options.text: Tell how fast you are traveling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell how fast you are traveling.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly when changing lanes, turning, merging, and making tight moves. Do not use mirrors to check your speed.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and get sleep. This is the only safe action. Fighting fatigue is dangerous and can cause a crash. Don't rely on pills—they won't make you truly alert.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's behavior.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's behavior.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash with an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance. Wait for police to arrive and tell them what you saw.

questions.question: Rearward amplification is:

options.text: The noise coming from the back of a vehicle.
The number of trailers a truck can pull.

questions.explanation: Vehicles with trailers can roll over due to the "crack-the-whip" effect. This effect is caused by rearward amplification.

questions.question: Before operating a tank vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Check vapor recovery kits, if needed.
Remove a third of the fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check vapor recovery kits, if needed.
questions.explanation: Before operating a tank vehicle, check that all special equipment works safely. This includes vapor recovery kits, grounding and bonding cables, and emergency shut-off systems.
